flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Nav
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, find the Manage Account menu on the left. From the Manage Account view find the Configurations page. From the Configurations page use the navigation bar at the top to find the Lists subpage. A playbook adds a malicious IP to a reusable ____ that WAF and Gateway rules can reference. (IP List / Page Rule / Redirect List / Waiting Room) The flag is what malicious IPs can be added to in this specific context.

hints.description: Look for the reusable object type under <s1-label>Lists</s1-label>.

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Nav
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, find the Domains dropdown and select find the Overview page. From the Overview page, find the one-flare.com domain. Find the Security dropdown from the menus the left and go to Security Rules. What is the name of a Custom Rule a SOAR playbook could toggle to block an attacker? The flag is the name of the Custom Rule in place that can block an attacker.

hints.description: Read the custom-rules list; if empty, that's a finding.

flags.name: Flag 3 - Analytics
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, on the left hand side find Analytics. Select Account Analytics from the dropdown. Change the Absolute time range to see data from the last 30 days. Account Analytics shows you an overview of traffic for all domains under your Cloudflare account, such as requests and bandwidth by country, information related to security, cache, and errors, among others. The flag is the country with the 3rd highest number of requests.

hints.description:
Make sure the <s1-label>Absolute time range</s1-label> is set to 30 days.

The flag is the country with the highest request volume out of the 4 options (3rd highest overall).

flags.name: Flag 4 - Analytics
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, on the left hand side find Analytics. Select HTTP Traffic from the dropdown. Change the Absolute time range to see data from the last 30 days. In the context of web traffic monitoring, a Referer is the webpage that linked to the resource being requested. In other words, it is inbound traffic from a link. So if a visitor to example.com clicks a link to your site there, the request will include a Referer header saying they came via example.com. The flag is the Referer with the highest request volume.

hints.description: The flag is under the <s1-label>Requests by volume source</s1-label> section of the page, under <s1-label>Referers</s1-label>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - Soledrop
flags.description: Enter shop.soledrop.co into a web browser. Once there, find the Status page. Cloudflare uses Bot Scores to measure the likelihood that an incoming web request is operated by an automated bot rather than a human. A bot score of 1 indicates the highest probability of bot activity, while a bot score of 99 indicates human activity. The flag is the bot score attributed to the activity on shop.soledrop.co.

hints.description: On Soledrop's <s1-label>Status</s1-label> page, the <s1-value>bot score</s1-value> is detailed under the 1st section of the <s1-label>Attack Timeline</s1-label>.

flags.name: Flag 6 - Bot score
flags.description: Go to Cloudflare's documentation on bot scores here: http://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/ Cloudflare uses Bot Scores to measure the likelihood that an incoming web request is operated by an automated bot rather than a human. A bot score of 1 indicates the highest probability of bot activity, while a bot score of 99 indicates human activity. See bot score calculation here for more info: http://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/. The flag is the category a bot score of 24 would fall under.

flags.description:
<s1-nav>In the SentinelOne console, navigate over to Event Search.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
The lookback window is the period of time Event Search will look back on and show logs for. A time of 24 hours means that Event Search will show you results for anything matching your query, but only from within the past 24 hours.

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the default time range for Event Search.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 9 - Data ingest
flags.description:
<s1-nav>In the SentinelOne console, navigate over to Event Search. Make sure the query is empty and the range is set to the last 72 hours. Type dataSource.vendor into the fields search bar and select Cloudflare.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
With Logpush enabled, Cloudflare can send all the relevant logs to the SentinelOne console for triage and response. Logpush can be configured to handle all sorts of volumes to fit the specific needs of your SOC team.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="10,000">The flag is the approximate number of logs coming from Cloudflare.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 10 - Detection
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate over to Detections. Find the detection associated with Credential stuffing</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Detections are a feature of SentinelOne that allow you to create queries that are applied to all incoming traffic. If a log or set of logs match the pattern they are aggregated into an alert for the SOC team to analyze.

Find the detection associated with Credential Stuffing.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="Single Event">The flag is the Rule Type associated with this detection.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 11 - Detection
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate over to Detections. Find the detection associated with Credential stuffing. Click on the Event Search button inside the detection window.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
When you use Event Search while inside a detection, the Event Search query is automatically populated with the query the detection was using. This allows analysts to save time and find the exact logs and events they are looking for.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is how many failed login attempts have occurred for the most recent event.</s1-flag>

hints.description: Make sure the lookback window is set to 72 hours and the Detection name is "CF-Access-CredStuffing — Login Brute Force / Credential Stuffing on portal.soledrop.co". The flag is under the failed_logins column.

flags.name: Flag 14 - Event Search Evidence
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to Event Search. Clear the search and set the search window to 72 hours.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Paste this DNS Tunneling search query into the event search.

class_uid=4003 dataSource.cloudflare_dataset='Gateway DNS' unmapped.QueryName=*
| let fqdn        = lower(unmapped.QueryName)
| let label       = replace(fqdn, '\\..*', '')
| let zone        = replace(fqdn, '^.*\\.([^.]+\\.[^.]+\\.[^.]+)$', '$1')
| let label_len   = len(label)
| let digit_cnt   = len(replace(label, '[^0-9]', ''))
| let digit_ratio = label_len > 0 ? digit_cnt / label_len : 0
| let is_txt      = query.type in:anycase ('txt')
| let src_ip      = src_endpoint.ip
| let host        = device.name
| group
    total_queries = count(),
    uniq_labels   = estimate_distinct(label),
    max_label_len = max(label_len),
    long_labels   = count(label_len >= 40),
    txt_long      = count(is_txt AND label_len >= 20),
    hi_entropy    = count(label_len >= 12 AND digit_ratio >= 0.15),
    device_uid    = any(device.uid),
    evidence      = max_by(unmapped.QueryName, label_len),
    first_seen    = oldest(timestamp),
    last_seen     = newest(timestamp)
  by src_ip, host, zone
| filter (hi_entropy >= 10 AND uniq_labels >= 10) OR (long_labels >= 5 AND uniq_labels >= 5) OR txt_long >= 3
| let reason = txt_long >= 3 ? 'Data-in-DNS exfil (TXT long labels)' : ((long_labels >= 5 AND uniq_labels >= 5) ? 'Long-label DNS tunneling' : 'DGA / high-entropy beaconing')
| let detection_time = simpledateformat(last_seen, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss z', 'America/Chicago')
| sort -uniq_labels
| columns detection_time, src_ip, host, zone, reason, total_queries, uniq_labels, long_labels, txt_long, hi_entropy, max_label_len, evidence, device_uid, first_seen
| limit 100

Detection queries can produce Evidence. Evidence is the key piece of data that caused the detection rule to fire. In this case the evidence is the DNS label, and it is indicative of a tunneling attack.

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890c2tunnel.acmecorp-lab.workers.dev">The flag is the string + domain that is cited as evidence. </s1-flag>
